content.text:
I submitted **index 18** (Co 0.33 / Sb 0.67, which is close to the CoSb₂O₆ composition) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, but the value is only 8.4×10⁻⁴ %. That is barely above zero, so I can't say whether any part of this line actually works as a photoanode.

| Index | Sb fraction | Why I picked it | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18 | 0.674 | CoSb₂O₆ is on the stability hull (MACE: 0 eV/atom above hull) | 8.4×10⁻⁴ |
| 5 | 0.235 | Co₇Sb₂O₁₂ spinel is near-stable (0.03 eV/atom) with a 1.44 eV predicted gap, low enough to absorb at 2.4 eV | −6.5×10⁻³ |
| 28 | 0.865 | Least-explored end of the line and the Gaussian-process model's top pick | 7.1×10⁻⁴ |

Things to keep in mind:
- **Weak evidence:** the gap between index 18 and index 28 is small, and I only covered three points out of 29. With every value this close to zero, the ranking may just reflect noise.
- **Distrusted gap prediction:** MEGNet predicted a 0.37 eV band gap for CoSb₂O₆. That seemed implausibly low for this kind of cobalt oxide, so I ignored it.
- **XRD not used:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never confirmed which crystal phases are actually present at the measured points.
